name: Joaquina
summary: A non-magmatic, fault-hosted system 30km northeast of Guatemala City, with over 70 hot/boiling springs and 15 fumaroles mapped across a 1km² thermal area plus adjacent manifestations. Shallow boreholes (20–200m) intersected pressurized boiling water and steam, and silica/cation geothermometry and fluid-inclusion studies consistently point to a 175–185°C+ resource at depth. Upflow is structurally controlled by a dilational step-over on a NE-striking fault, with heat sourced from deep circulation along structures related to the Motagua Fault system rather than nearby volcanism. Preliminary resource-capacity estimates centre on a mean of ~28 MWe.
